AzureOpenAI.//ApiKey: SECRET (ADR 0017), never committed. Arrives as AzureOpenAI__ApiKey — a Container App secret in prod (AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY GitHub secret), user secrets locally. It authenticates BOTH the Foundry chat/Responses provider (which inherits it, see Models:Providers:foundry) and the embedding client — one source of truth. Unlike the third-party provider keys, this is the availability path: a blank key is FATAL at startup, not skipped.

Models.//: Model providers (ADR 0013). A model is named by a QUALIFIED id, 'provider:model', split on the FIRST colon — GitHub's own ids contain a slash (openai/gpt-4o-mini), so a slash separator would have been ambiguous. An id with no colon is a legacy id and resolves against the default provider's namespace, which is why this needed no state migration.
Models.//Default: The default model is deliberately NOT set here. Left empty, it is derived as 'foundry:<AzureOpenAI:DeploymentName>' — the key Bicep threads in as AzureOpenAI__DeploymentName. Hardcoding 'foundry:gpt-4o' here would silently override that env var and make the Bicep param dead config: it would look authoritative and change nothing. Same inheritance rule as the foundry provider's Endpoint below. Set this only to default to a NON-Foundry model, which would mean defaulting to a third-party endpoint — see the ADR before you do.

foundry.//: Declares NO Endpoint/SubscriptionId/ResourceGroup/AccountName/ApiKey on purpose: it inherits them from the AzureOpenAI:* keys above (endpoint, key, ARM coords), which Bicep threads in as env vars and the embedding client also reads. One source of truth. ApiKey (ADR 0017) is the availability path — a blank one is FATAL at startup, unlike a third-party provider key. Discover is FALSE because an Azure OpenAI data-plane KEY cannot authenticate ARM (ADR 0017 dropped MI discovery); the picker therefore offers EXACTLY the Models declared below, not a live ARM enumeration. The default deployment (AzureOpenAI:DeploymentName, gpt-5.4) MUST be one of them — the catalog only synthesizes the default when nothing is declared, so a default missing from this non-empty list vanishes from the picker. Add a deployment by adding it to Models here, and keep this list in sync with AzureOpenAI:DeploymentName. A SECOND Foundry account is added by declaring its own Endpoint (+ its own ApiKey) on a new provider key — no code change.
foundry.//UseResponsesApi: ADR 0014/0015/0017. ON: every model of this provider runs the OpenAI Responses API statelessly (store=false) via {endpoint}/openai/v1 with an api-key header carrying the Azure OpenAI key (ADR 0017 replaced ADR 0014's managed-identity bearer), instead of Chat Completions — and reaches OpenAI's hosted web_search + code_interpreter tools, replacing the SearXNG shims (ADR 0011 stays for any Chat-path model). This sends EVERY conversation through the Responses surface. Verified against THIS endpoint (agent42.services.ai.azure.com/openai/v1) with the resource KEY — api-key-header auth, hosted web_search firing, store=false, deployment gpt-5.4 — spike-confirmed 2026-07-16. Turn OFF to revert to Chat Completions + SearXNG with no other change.

github.//: GitHub Models. ApiKey is a SECRET and is never committed: it arrives as Models__Providers__github__ApiKey, from a Container App secret in prod (GITHUB_MODELS_TOKEN GitHub secret). Absent is a supported state — the provider is skipped with a warning and the app boots on Foundry alone. THIS SENDS CONVERSATION CONTENT TO A THIRD PARTY, outside the Entra tenant: document excerpts, image SAS URLs and the user's street address (ADR 0013 Consequences). SupportsTools/SupportsVision are per-model and were MEASURED, not assumed — phi-4 and DeepSeek, for instance, do not call tools. Per-request input caps are small (16k for gpt-4o/gpt-4.1, 8k for the minis) and a request over the cap fails with HTTP 413, not 400.

WebSearch.//: The SearXNG sidecar in the same Container App. Containers in one Container App share a network namespace, so it is reached over localhost; 8888 because the backend's own ingress already owns 8080. Overridden by WebSearch__Endpoint in Bicep and by the AppHost locally.

Geocoding.//: Reverse geocoding for the get_current_location tool (ADR 0012). GoogleApiKey is a SECRET and is never committed: it arrives as Geocoding__GoogleApiKey, from a Container App secret in prod (GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY GitHub secret) or user secrets locally. Absent is a supported state — the tool then reports coordinates with no street address, and the app starts normally.
